pie: h₂nér h₁eǵóh₂ gʰóstis. stégesi toy ḱósyeh₂i kʷsépi sésoh₂. gʰóstey ḱóm ḱóymom mē wéyḱs. móros dṓm déms h₁éyti. kʷís wos h₁ím sélǵt? deywṓs gʰrémonti. h₁néwn̥ wiHrṓs h₃r̥gént. nu pró h₁éyoh₂. diwyṓs te ph₂sih₁ént. stóygʰoy te h₂léksoyh₁ent.
english: Man, I am a guest. Let me sleep under your roof on this night. Do not enter this village, stranger. A plague goes from house to house. Who sent it to you? The gods are angry. Nine men have perished. Then I shall go onward. May the heavenly ones guard you. May they protect you on the road.

pie: kʷŕ̥mey h₁éǵʰs h₁néwn̥ wr̥míbʰis ḱóm gʷh₂dʰí. kʷŕ̥mey snéh₁wōr mosgʰṓd ih₂dʰí. wórmey mḗms sn̥h₁wénbʰos h₁idʰí. nu skéwHtim mémsos sérpe. kʷŕ̥mey soksóm skuHtéys litdʰí. nu kʷŕ̥mey h₂én mr̥dʰí h₂éti-kʷe mē gʷéms.
english: Go out, worm, with nine worms! Go, worm, from the marrow into the sinews! Go, worm, from the sinews into the flesh! Now crawl from the flesh into the skin! Go away, worm, from the skin into the stone! Now die there, worm, and do not come back!

pie: tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis h₂aǵróm bʰuged.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: mógʰus swérgʰoy légʰyet h₁ésyo-kʷe úderos h₂idnéwt. h₁ésyo méh₂tēr ǵn̥h₃réh₂m séneh₂m gʷénh₂m̥ wédʰet. séh₂ h₁ím spéḱyet h₂éǵt-kʷe. kʷŕ̥mis h₁ésmi h₁n̥dóm tḱéyti. kéh₂nmn̥ h₁néwn̥ nókʷtn̥s kh₂nét. nu kʷŕ̥mis h₁ésyo h₁h₃sés h₁nédʰt. h₁ím soksóh₁ mélh₂t h₁ím-kʷe péh₂wr̥ Hyéh₁kt. mógʰus bʰéwdʰt h₂mélǵos-kʷe péh₃t. ǵénh₁trih₂ ǵn̥h₃réh₂ey káprom déh₃t.
english: A boy was lying in sickness, and his belly was swelling. His mother brought a wise old woman. She looked at him, and she spoke. A worm dwells inside him. For nine nights she chanted the song. Then the worm came forth from his mouth. She ground it with a stone, and she threw it into the fire. The boy woke up and drank milk. The mother gave the wise one a goat.

pie: wóyḱe moy ǵr̥h₂nóm dh₃dʰí. dʰugh₂téres moy gʷoldʰóh₁ mr̥yóntor. péh₂urom ǵr̥h₂nóm méǵʰye h₁ésti. népotes moy kénkonti. sémeh₂i te gʰéldʰōh₂. nu bʰoh₂góm h₁áyso. h₂élyoybʰos mē wéwkes. príHe toy deywṓs h₁wésuh₂ dh₃ih₁ént.
english: Neighbour, give me grain. My daughters are dying of hunger. I have little grain. My grandsons are hungry. I shall repay you in the summer. Then take a share. Do not tell the others. May the gods give you good things, friend.

pie: kʷíd toy wóyḱe stéh₂dʰh₁om h₂éǵrōs légʰeti? swérgʰos h₁íd h₁épt. tísres gʷówes dʰǵʰyés h₃l̥h₁ént. kʷíd dʰédʰeh₁esi? n̥ḱéwih₂n̥s ph₂wéni h₁éwsōh₂. swóm stéh₂dʰh₁om h₂epó h₂éǵe. h₁íd pérwr̥ h₁élh₂oh₂. n̥mr̥tṓs nos ph₂sih₁ént.
english: Neighbour, why does your herd lie in the pasture? A sickness has seized it. Three cows perished yesterday. What will you do? I shall burn the dead ones in the fire. Drive your own herd away! I shall drive it to the mountain. May the immortals guard us.

pie: príHe gʷíh₃wesi. ǵʰyémi te ne widóm. gʷíh₃woh₂ méh₂tēr-kʷe moy h₃érgt. dwóh₁ moy suHnúh₁ mr̥tóh₁. ph₂tḗr moy snóygʷʰom h₁éǵʰs gʷéh₂t ne-kʷe nést. téḱnoybʰos swóm mā́dsom déh₃t. h₁éy h₁wésus wiHrós h₁ést. wósr̥ gʷegʷóme. h₂éǵrons séh₁yōmes. séh₁yōmes néḱuns-kʷe meménomes.
english: Friend, you are alive! I did not see you in the winter. I am alive, and my mother perished. My two sons are dead. My father went out into the snow, and he did not return home. He gave his own food to the children. He was a good man. The spring has come. Let us sow the fields. Let us sow, and let us remember the dead.

pie: h₁óyneh₂i sémeh₂i ne h₂wérst. déh₂nuh₂ térst gʰréh₁mn̥-kʷe h₂sowsóm bʰúHt. péḱu bʰr̥h₁wéni sth₂éh₁yet wódr̥-kʷe ne widét. h₃rḗǵs woyḱóns dʰh₁tléh₂m wédʰet. h₂réh₁dʰont. pérkʷunōy méǵistom uksénm̥ déh₃omes. uksénm̥ h₂ḱméni gʷʰnént dʰuh₂mós-kʷe dyḗm úd bʰwéh₂t. nu pérkʷunos stonh₂éyet h₂wérst-kʷe. mórtōs méwdont.
english: In one summer it did not rain. The rivers dried up, and the grass became dry. The cattle stood at the spring, and they did not find water. The king led the villagers to the assembly. They took counsel. Let us give the greatest bull to Perkʷunos. They slew the bull on the stone, and the smoke arose to the sky. Then Perkʷunos thundered, and it rained. The people rejoiced.

pie: pótey mḗms lelóykʷe. péh₂ureh₂ dʰoHnéh₂ méneti. nu nos népotes dʰugh₂téres-kʷe h₁íh₂m̥ h₂éḱh₃onti. túH h₁eǵóh₂-kʷe kénkōwos. sénos toy ph₂tḗr ne gʷr̥h₃ḗti? pl̥h₁éwih₂n̥s ǵʰéyomn̥s dérḱt. pótey gʷíh₃wōnti. gʷíh₃woyh₁ent.
english: Husband, the meat is gone. A little grain remains. Then our grandsons and daughters shall eat it. You and I shall be hungry. Shall your old father not eat? He has seen many winters. They will live, husband. May they live.

pie: tat kukruwants awis agram ā bʰugat.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: pótni dʰégʷʰoh₂. wódr̥ moy dh₃dʰí. wíHre ph₃dʰí. gʷʰéros te léykʷeti. mr̥tóm moy bʰréh₂term̥ kʷsépi kʷéḱm̥. ḱód mē mléwHs. nu ssdʰí. bʰéh₂t moy dʰwóri-kʷe sth₂éh₁yet. dʰwórm̥ h₂léksōh₂. néḱewes h₁idʰé ne wéyḱonti.
english: Wife, I am burning. Give me water. Drink, husband. The heat will leave you. In the night I caught sight of my dead brother. Do not say this. Sleep now. He spoke to me, and he was standing at the door. I shall protect the door. The dead will not come in here.

pie: kʷíd nos deywṓs mórom sl̥ǵént? h₁éymos dh₂pnósyo bʰoh₂góm ne dh₃mé. dyḗws gʰrémeti. nu kʷíd h₁éymos dédeh₃omes? h₁éymos méǵh₂m̥ uksénm̥ h₁néwn̥-kʷe káprons dédeh₃omes. nu móros léyteti? h₁yód nos n̥mr̥tṓs ḱléwonti léyteti.
english: Why did the gods send the plague to us? We did not give them a share of the feast. Dyēus is angry. What shall we give them now? Let us give them a big bull and nine goats. Will the plague go away then? If the immortals hear us, it will go away.

pie: swérgʰos ugʷséni h₁ésti. h₁ím moréyōmes h₁ésyo-kʷe mḗms h₂éḱh₃omes? tósyo ugʷsnés mḗms mē h₂éḱh₃s. swérgʰos twé h₁n̥dó wéyḱeti. kʷíd dʰédʰeh₁omes? h₁ím moréye h₁ím-kʷe ph₂wéni h₁éwse. stéh₂dʰh₁om h₁ésyo dʰuh₂móm mē h₃édoyh₁t. ḱód dʰédʰeh₁oh₂.
english: A sickness is in the ox. Shall we kill it and eat its meat? Do not eat the meat of that ox. The sickness will go into you. What shall we do? Kill it, and burn it in the fire. May the herd not smell its smoke. I shall do this.

pie: kʷíd péh₂ure súHnew ne h₁gérs? h₂mélǵos moy wékʷsperoy pstnés péh₃t. nu túH ḱolHtós h₂ewsér h₁és. gʷoldʰós te sléh₂gʷt ne-kʷe me sléh₂gʷt. HréwdHmi-ge ph₂tḗr-kʷe toy HréwdHti. súHnew moy sríHǵesi ḱéyso.
english: Little son, why did you not wake? In the evening you drank milk from my breast. Then at dawn you were cold. Hunger took you, and it did not take me. I weep indeed, and your father weeps. Lie, my son, in the cold.

pie: h₁ést ǵʰéymn̥ dl̥h₁gʰóm gʷoldʰós-kʷe dl̥h₁gʰós h₁ést. nu kʷsépes ḱolHtéh₂es h₁sént. ǵr̥h₂nóm néḱt gʷówes-kʷe gʷowsth₂óysu h₃r̥gént. dórwih₁ lowbʰóm gʷr̥h₃óme ḱwónn̥s h₂ḱh₃mé. ǵérh₂ontes sríHgos úd stéygʰont ne n̥sént. kʷís ǵérh₂ontn̥s gʷr̥néHeti? wéy gʷih₃wṓs h₁íns gʷr̥néHomes.
english: Long was the winter, and long was the hunger. Then the nights were cold. The grain vanished, and the cattle perished in the stalls. We devoured the bark of the trees, we ate the dogs. The old men walked out into the frost, they did not return home. Who will praise the old men? We, the living, shall praise them.

pie: séna toy gʷḗn péḱu gʷíh₃weti péḱu-kʷe nos mr̥yétor. h₃ókʷ toy h₂egʰóm. h₃ókʷ moy ne h₂egʰóm. deywṓs stéh₂dʰh₁oybʰos mórom sl̥ǵént. nu toy kʷíd stéh₂dʰh₁om gʷíh₃weti? h₁íd pérwr̥ h₂éǵoh₂ wódr̥-kʷe wos ne píph₃eti. nu nos stéh₂dʰh₁om h₂én h₁élh₂omes.
english: Old woman, your cattle live, and our cattle die. Your eye is evil. My eye is not evil. The gods sent the plague to the herds. Why then does your herd live? I drive it to the mountain, and it does not drink your water. Then we shall drive our herd there.

pie: nu wos déywōs ḱóm ugʷsénm̥ dedh₃més. mórom stégesbʰos h₂pó sl̥h₂gʷté. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓd mr̥yóntor sénōs mr̥yóntor. ń̥mr̥tōs nos mē gʰrémete. móros-ge nos póyḱons gʷh₂yéh₁t.
english: Gods, now we give you this ox. Take the plague away from the houses! The young are dying, the old ones are dying. Immortals, do not rage at us! May the plague indeed go to our enemies.

pie: nu gʷʰéros ḱósmōd h₂n̥rés h₂epó gʷh₂dʰí. gʷʰéros dweh₂réh₂ pérwōr h₁r̥sḱé. nu wĺ̥kʷons h₁éwse h₂éḱmonn̥s-kʷe h₁éwse. gʷʰéros ḱóm h₂nérm̥ mē h₁éwses. nu krépos kéh₂ilom bʰuHyéh₁t. nu h₂ewsér sth₂yéh₁t ph₃yéh₁t-kʷe.
english: Now, heat, go away from this man! Go, heat, to the far mountains! Now burn the wolves, and burn the stones! Do not burn this man, heat! Now may the body become whole. Then at dawn may he stand up and drink.

pie: nu h₂egʰóm h₃ókʷ stéh₂dʰh₁ōd litdʰí. h₃ókʷ soksóm wódr̥-kʷe wiḱdʰí. nu h₂egʰóm h₃ókʷ wí bʰindih₁h₂é. wetsṓs nos kéh₂ilōs h₁sih₁ént. nu diwyṓs gʷowsth₂óm ph₂sih₁ént.
english: Now, evil eye, go away from the herd! Enter the stone and the water, eye! Now may the evil eye burst asunder. May our calves be healthy. Now may the heavenly ones guard the stall.

pie: ḱm̥tóm h₂óweyes poh₂imnéy h₁sént. swérgʰos h₁íh₂n̥s h₁óynoy ǵʰiméni h₁ludʰét. kʷéh₂sont l̥gʰént-kʷe ne-kʷe sth₂ént. poh₂imḗn n̥ḱéwih₂n̥s méǵh₂i h₂éydʰoy h₁éwset. déḱm̥ h₂óweyes ménont. só h₁íh₂n̥s pérwr̥ h₁élh₂t. h₁sént h₂egʷnṓs sémeh₂i. poh₂imḗn n̥mr̥tóns gʷr̥néHt.
english: A shepherd had a hundred sheep. In one winter a sickness arrived among them. They coughed, and they lay down, and they did not stand up. The shepherd burned the dead ones in a great fire. Ten sheep remained. He drove them to the mountain. In the summer there were lambs. The shepherd praised the immortals.

pie: snóygʷʰos tósyeh₂i ǵʰyémi moḱs péth₁t. stéh₂dʰh₁eh₂ gʰréh₁mn̥ ne widét ugʷsénes-kʷe gʷowsth₂óysu h₃r̥gént. nu mórtōs h₁éysōm mḗms gʷr̥h₃ónt. dʰoHnéh₂ kʷéroybʰos néḱt. nu gʷoldʰós ḱóymom h₁ért. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs kʷspsú HrudHént ǵénh₁trih₂es-kʷe kʷid h₁éymos ne dédh₃n̥t. nu sémeh₂ h₁ludʰét péh₂ureh₂es-kʷe h₂óweyes gʷih₃wéh₂es h₁sént.
english: In that winter the snow fell early. The herds did not find grass, and the oxen perished in the stalls. Then the people devoured their flesh. The grain vanished from the pots. Then hunger arrived in the village. The young ones wept in the nights, and the mothers gave them nothing. Then the summer arrived, and few sheep were alive.

pie: pótey ḱóm ḱóymom léykʷomes. móros h₁idʰé tḱéyti. kúdʰe ǵʰyémi téḱnōys ḱóm yéh₂omes? bʰréh₂tr̥s moy dṓm h₂ewsér yéh₂omes. bʰréh₂tr̥s toy dṓm dweh₂rós. steh₂rṓs h₂én ne stéygʰōnti. nu h₁íns bʰérōmes. kʷís nos pótni bʰérēti? ménōmes diwyṓs-kʷe h₂réh₁dʰoyh₁ent.
english: Husband, let us leave this village. The plague dwells here. Where shall we go with the children in the winter? Let us go toward the dawn, to the house of my brother. The house of your brother is far. The old ones will not walk there. Then we shall carry them. And who will carry us, wife? Let us stay, and may the heavenly ones decide.

pie: h₁ést séneh₂ gʷḗn. swṓy suHnówey gʷoldʰóy h₂éǵt. súHnew me sríHgos h₁éǵʰs wédʰe. h₁ḗdmi ne-kʷe wr̥ǵyóh₂. só HréwdHt h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe nékʷti h₂epó wédʰet. dréwi Hn̥dʰí sédt ne-kʷe wérh₁t. h₁éy h₂éyeri néseto. h₁íh₂ ḱolHtéh₂ h₁ést ne-kʷe h₂énh₁t. h₁ésyeh₂s népotes gʷih₃wṓs h₁sént.
english: There was an old woman. In the hunger she spoke to her son. Lead me out into the cold, son. I eat, and I do not work. He wept, and he led her away in the night. She sat down under a tree, and she did not speak. In the morning he returned. She was cold, and she did not breathe. But her grandsons were alive.

pie: ǵʰwḗrm̥ bʰérǵʰoysu réh₁ts? ne kʷid réh₁tm̥. wĺ̥kʷōs ǵʰwḗrn̥s gʷr̥h₃ént. wĺ̥kʷōs éti kénkonti? kénkonti. gʰórdʰom nékʷti h₁ludʰónt. nu h₂yuHn̥ḱóns ph₂sdʰí. wĺ̥kʷoybʰos bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e. h₁íns ḱwn̥bʰís péh₂soh₂.
english: Did you find a beast in the hills? I found nothing. The wolves devoured the beasts. Are the wolves hungry too? They are hungry. In the night they arrived at the fence. Then guard the young ones. I am afraid of the wolves. I shall guard them with the dogs.

pie: ph₂ter dʰéǵʰōm góleti. kʷíh₁ h₁íh₂m̥ dʰélbʰomes? méh₂term̥ toy snóygʷʰoy logʰéyōmes h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe h₂ḱmn̥bʰís stégōmes. wĺ̥kʷōs h₁íh₂m̥ winédonti. h₁íh₂m̥ ne winédonti. h₂éḱmones méǵh₂es. h₁yód sémeh₂ gʷm̥yḗti h₁íh₂m̥ dʰǵʰémi logʰéyōmes. nu h₁ésyeh₂ey kéh₂nmn̥ séngʷʰōmes.
english: Father, the earth is frozen. How shall we dig it? Let us lay your mother in the snow, and let us cover her with stones. The wolves will find her. They will not find her. The stones are big. When the summer comes, we shall lay her in the earth. Then we shall sing a song for her.

pie: súHnew me sríHgos ḱósyeh₂i nékʷti h₁éǵʰs bʰére. kʷíd ḱód mléwHsi? h₁eǵóh₂ ǵérh₂onts n̥ptṓm-kʷe moy mā́dsom gʷr̥h₃óh₂. sríHǵesi te ne léykʷoh₂. gʷoldʰós népotn̥s h₁épt. sríHgos me sl̥h₂gʷyéh₁t h₁íns-kʷe mē sl̥h₂gʷyéh₁t. HréwdHmi bʰérōh₂-kʷe te.
english: Son, carry me out into the frost on this night. Why do you say this? I am old, and I devour the food of my grandsons. I shall not leave you in the cold. Hunger has seized the grandsons. May the cold take me, and may it not take them. I weep, and I shall carry you.

pie: kʷŕ̥mins ḱósmi téḱnoy gʷʰénmi. wórmins úderoy widéh₁yoh₂. méǵh₂s kʷr̥méyōm h₃rḗǵs mr̥tós. ǵénh₁trih₂ h₃élh₁t bʰréh₂tēr-kʷe éti h₃érgt. nu h₁ésyo swésōr n̥ḱéwih₂. kʷŕ̥mins gʷr̥h₂unéh₁ mélh₂mi. nu téḱnom bʰudʰdʰí h₂n̥h₁dʰí-kʷe.
english: I slay the worms in this child. I see the worms in the belly. The great king of the worms is dead. The mother perished, and the brother perished too. Now his sister is dead. I grind the worms with the millstone. Now wake, child, and breathe!

pie: owis eḱwōs kʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses
